cards.explanation: The answer is True. Solomon, Israel's king, says it to the LORD: “But I have built You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever.” An exalted house, a place to dwell forever: that's exactly how he puts it, friends.

The answer is Solomon's father David. Solomon, Israel's king, says the LORD spoke this promise “…to my father David…” So Solomon is standing inside a promise his own dad received, and the LORD fulfilled it with His own hand. The promise was spoken, and now it's built, friends.

The answer is Jerusalem, friends! The LORD says, “But now I have chosen Jerusalem for My Name to be there, and I have chosen David to be over My people Israel.” A city and a king, chosen side by side. Before that, He hadn't chosen any city from any tribe.

The answer is that David did well to have it in his heart. The LORD tells David, “…you have done well to have this in your heart.” David wasn't going to be the builder, but the LORD still praised the desire. I've had plenty of plans in my heart that never made it out of the dough, so I love that, friends.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says to David, “…you are not the one to build it; but your son, your own offspring, will build the house for My Name.” David had the idea, and his own son gets the job. The word “Nevertheless” is the turn in that sentence.

The answer is the ark holding the LORD's covenant, friends! Solomon says, “And there I have placed the ark, which contains the covenant of the LORD that He made with the children of Israel.” The ark is the thing he places in the house. And the ark contains the covenant of the LORD.

The answer is that he kneels and spreads his hands toward heaven. On the platform, Solomon “…knelt down before the whole assembly of Israel, spread out his hands toward heaven…” The king gets down on his knees in front of everyone. I think that tells you where his heart is, friends.

The answer is False, friends. Solomon starts with “O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven or on earth…” No other gods get a mention. The prayer starts with who the LORD is, and the covenant He keeps comes right after.

The answer is law, friends! The promise comes “…if only your descendants guard their way to walk in My law as you have walked before Me.” The throne promise comes with the condition of walking in that law.

The answer is even the highest heavens, friends! Solomon says, “The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built.” If the highest heavens can't contain God, then this temple can't either. That's how Solomon puts it.
The answer is True, friends. Solomon prays, “May Your eyes be open toward this temple day and night…” Day and night, no breaks. He asks the LORD to hear the prayer prayed toward that place.

The answer is from heaven, where He dwells, friends! Solomon asks, “May You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place.” Israel prays toward the temple, and Solomon asks the LORD to hear from heaven. It matches what he said about the highest heavens.
The answer is forgive, friends! Solomon prays, “May You hear and forgive.” Hear, then forgive. I'd like both of those on every day of my life.

The answers are wicked in the first blank and righteous in the second, friends. Solomon asks the LORD to judge, “…condemning the wicked man by bringing down on his own head what he has done…” What he did comes back on his own head. Then Solomon asks God to be “…justifying the righteous man by rewarding him according to his righteousness.” So the judgment goes both ways, and the righteous man gets rewarded.

The answer is that they have sinned against God, friends. Solomon says Israel is defeated “…because they have sinned against You…” He names the reason out loud. Then he says they return, confess God's name, and pray in the temple.

The answer is False, friends. Solomon asks God to hear from heaven and forgive, then says, “May You restore them to the land You gave to them and their fathers.” It's the same land, not a new one. Forgiveness comes first, and then the restoring.

The answer is the good way they should walk, friends! Solomon asks God to forgive them “…so that You may teach them the good way in which they should walk.” Both are requests: forgive and teach. After that, he asks God to send rain on the land.
The answer is hearts, friends! Solomon says, “…You alone know the hearts of men…” Only God knows what's in every heart. That's why he asks Him to forgive and repay each man.

The answer is that all peoples will know His name and fear Him, friends! Solomon says, “Then all the peoples of the earth will know Your name and fear You, as do Your people Israel…” It's the whole world, not just Israel. They'll know the house is called by God's Name too.

The answer is True, friends. Solomon asks, “…then may You hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and may You uphold their cause.” They pray toward the city and the temple, and he asks God to hear from heaven. He asks God to uphold their cause.

The answer is captives, friends. Solomon pictures an enemy “…who takes them as captives to a land far or near…” That's a heavy picture. I think it makes the next part, where they come to their senses and return, matter even more.

The answer is True, friends. Solomon says that in the land of their enemies, when they return to God with all their heart and soul, they pray “…in the direction of the land that You gave to their fathers, the city You have chosen, and the house I have built for Your Name…” Even from far away, their prayer is aimed at those places.

The answer is His resting place, friends! Solomon prays, “Now therefore, arise, O LORD God, and enter Your resting place, You and the ark of Your might.” The ark goes in with Him. It's a big way to close out the prayer.
